newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: PDVSA may look at Orinoco oil "beauty contest".
newsitem.headline: PDVSA may look at Orinoco oil "beauty contest".

text.p: Venezuela's state oil company Petroleos de Venezuela (PDVSA) may consider some form of beauty contest to choose future partners in Orinoco extra-heavy crude oil joint-ventures, a senior official said on Thursday.
Juan Szabo, PDVSA's exploration and production chief, said a new subsidiary handling the area should be up and running by October and it would decide on the new policy.

"We do think that if we have more interested parties than areas we want to develop, we would need some sort of beauty contest, some sort of selection process which would be competitive, but we have not decided that at all yet," he told Reuters by telephone.

The new subsidiary is part of a PDVSA-wide restructuring to create focused business units. PDVSA has already signed four Orinoco deals worth $13 billion, was in advanced negotiations with Exxon and Coastal on two more worth $4 billion, and was in the early stages of talks on a few more, he said.
The projects are so capital intensive because they involve drilling wells, laying pipelines and building conversion plants to change the extra-heavy oil into something resembling traditional crude.
The first such contract, signed with Conoco, prompted a wave of interest in the concept that has become economically and technically viable only in recent years.
The four ventures signed so far aim to produce 620,000 barrel per day of oil, but the Orinoco could pump much more than that given its 270 billion barrel recoverable reserves.
"We are talking to BP, Texaco, Shell -- several companies -- but there's nothing signed nor any agreement yet," he said.
